title: Deferred Fixed Annuities Contract Provisions: Partial Withdrawals
content:
Partial withdrawal provisions of Ashgrove Deferred Fixed Annuities. The owner may take partial withdrawals by signed request.

## Conditions of payment

A partial withdrawal is paid only where the system records show both of the following for the contract and the request concerned:

| Condition | What the records must show |
|---|---|
| Contract status | A withdrawal is paid only while the contract status is active — the status on the record of the contract the withdrawal is taken from. |
| Signed request | A partial withdrawal is paid only on a withdrawal request signed by the owner and approved — a withdrawal service request on that contract with its signed date and an approved status, the withdrawal being made under that request. |

A caller's account that a request was signed does not stand in for the record. The table states conditions without which no withdrawal is paid; it does not list everything a withdrawal is subject to.

## Amounts

1. Each withdrawal must be at least the tier's smallest partial withdrawal.
2. A request that would leave less than the tier's contract value that must remain after a partial withdrawal is processed as a full surrender.

## Free amount and excess

3. From the tier's first contract year of the free withdrawal amount, [*retired wording, no longer in force:* "withdrawals in a contract year up to the free withdrawal percentage of the contract value on the most recent contract anniversary"] (the initial premium in the first contract year) are free of surrender charge. Withdrawals already taken in the contract year use up the free amount: they are the total of withdrawals paid in the current contract year — which runs from the latest contract anniversary on or before the withdrawal, or from the issue date in contract year 1 — before the withdrawal being considered. Unused free amount carries forward only where the tier's carryover feature is yes.
4. The free amount still available is the free amount less the withdrawals already taken in the contract year, never below zero; the part of a withdrawal above it is an excess withdrawal, never below zero.
5. Within the tier's surrender charge period, counted from the start date of the current surrender charge schedule, the excess withdrawal [*retired wording, no longer in force:* "bears a surrender charge of that part times the surrender charge ladder percentage for the schedule year in which it is taken, rounded to the cent"]; the charge is deducted from the remaining contract value, not from the amount paid.
6. No surrender charge applies during a guarantee period renewal window, or to amounts waived under the nursing home and terminal illness waivers or under the required minimum distribution provisions.

The retired wording quoted in clauses 3 and 5 has been superseded by the current basis; the tier figures it names keep their values.

## Tax and withholding

7. On a non-qualified contract a withdrawal is taxable first to the extent of the gain, the gain being the contract value less the cost basis. On a traditional IRA or a SEP IRA the whole amount is taxable. On a Roth IRA no tax is withheld by default.
8. Federal tax is withheld at the federal withholding percentage of the taxable amount unless the owner elected no withholding.

## Worked illustrations (hypothetical figures)

- *Free amount still available.* Free amount $5000; withdrawals already taken this contract year $3000: $2000 remains free. A $2500 withdrawal then has an excess of $500. Had $6000 already been taken, nothing would remain free and the whole withdrawal would be excess.
- *Gain first.* Non-qualified contract, contract value $60000, cost basis $50000, gain $10000. A $4000 withdrawal is wholly taxable; a $12000 withdrawal is taxable on $10000. With withholding at 10% and no election against it, $400 and $1000 are withheld respectively.
- *IRA.* On a traditional IRA a $4000 withdrawal is taxable on the whole $4000.
